$comment: The named fixture corpus PRD 4.5 measures against, and the seeded revision pair its
chunk-reuse row asks for. Three documents, with a one-paragraph edit to the largest.
The corpus is this size on purpose. Chunk reuse is a ratio, so its resolution is one
over the number of chunks in the revised source: a six-chunk document quantises the
measurement to seventeen-point steps, and a 90% target is then not merely unmet but
unmeasurable. A document that chunks into roughly twenty is the smallest fixture on
which the target means anything. It was not sized to make the number pass — the test
records the measured ratio either way, and the target is never moved.
The chunking settings belong to the connector, not to the repository (PRD 4.3), which
is why they are stated here beside the corpus rather than as a default somewhere.
hardware: not stated: this fixture measures counts and ratios, which do not depend on it
